(a) Except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer, no driver of a vehicle shall make or attempt to make a turning movement prohibited by this section at the locations and during the days and times specified herein.
(b) The following turning movements are prohibited at all times:
(1) School property and Jackson Street. Vehicles leaving the parking lot of the school property shall not turn left to travel south onto Jackson Street.
(2) Richway and Old National Highway. Vehicles leaving the business premises of Richway, Inc. shall not turn left to travel north onto Old National Highway.
(c) The following turning movements are prohibited Monday through Friday on school days, during the hours of 6:45 a.m. to 7:45 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. to 4:15 p.m.:
(1) York Road and Lakeshore Drive. Vehicles traveling from York Road onto Lakeshore Drive shall not turn left.
(2) Lakeshore Drive and York Road. Vehicles traveling on Lakeshore Drive shall not turn left onto York Road.
(3) Glenda Drive and Lakeshore Drive. Vehicles traveling from Glenda Drive onto Lakeshore Drive shall not turn right.
(d) The turning restrictions established by subsection (c) shall apply only during the days and hours specified therein. At all other times, turning movements at such intersections shall be governed by otherwise applicable traffic laws and traffic-control devices.
(e) The chief of police, or the chief's designee, is authorized and directed to cause appropriate official traffic-control devices to be erected and maintained at each location subject to subsection (c), which devices shall provide reasonable notice of the prohibited turning movement and the applicable days and hours of the restriction.
(f) Consistent with O.C.G.A. § 40-6-371(c), no turning restriction established pursuant to subsection (c) shall become effective or enforceable until appropriate official traffic-control devices giving notice of the restriction have been erected at the affected location.
(g) Nothing in this section shall prohibit or otherwise limit a law enforcement officer from directing, controlling, or regulating traffic as otherwise authorized by law or this Code.

(a) The mayor and council may appoint not more than seven (7) persons to enforce the handicapped parking laws of the City of College Park. Each person so appointed shall be a citizen of the United States and of College Park, be of good moral character, and shall not have previously been convicted of a felony. In addition, each such person appointed shall be a handicapped person as defined in O.C.G.A. section 40-6-221(2).
(b) Each person appointed pursuant to this Code section shall submit an application to the city, and upon designation by the mayor and council, shall complete such training as directed by the chief of police and shall take and subscribe an oath of office as prescribed by the mayor and council.
(c) The application required by subsection (b) above shall include the name and address of the applicant; his citizenship; a statement of qualification as a handicapped person as that term is defined in O.C.G.A. section 40-6-221(2); and shall have attached to such application a two-inch by two-inch photograph of the applicant, together with a complete set of fingerprints.
(d) Upon receipt of the application, the chief of police or his designee shall cause a complete and thorough investigation to be made of the applicant's moral, physical and mental qualifications.
(e) Any person appointed and sworn as a handicapped parking enforcement officer shall have the power to serve citations for violations or failure to comply with handicapped parking laws of the City of College Park in the same manner as any law enforcement officer of the state or city, subject to the following limitations:
(1) No person so appointed shall be deemed a peace officer, nor shall such person be deemed an employee of the state, county or city, nor receive any compensation therefrom.
(2) No such appointed person shall be required to complete training as a peace officer.
(3) No such appointed person shall have the power or duty to enforce other traffic or criminal laws of the state or the city.
(4) No person so appointed shall possess or carry firearms or other weapons for the purpose of enforcing handicapped parking laws.
(5) No person so appointed shall be entitled to any indemnification from the state, county or city for any injury or property damage sustained as a result of his enforcement activities. (a) Purpose. The purpose of this section is to preserve the safe and reasonable use of residential streets and community areas by regulating the use of such areas for commercial fleet staging. Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit the lawful operation of a commercial fleet vehicle upon a public street or the immediate pickup or drop-off of a passenger at a lawful location.
(b) Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms shall have the meanings provided below:
(1) Commercial fleet operator means any person or entity that owns, leases, controls, dispatches, manages, or operates commercial fleet vehicles for the transportation of passengers for compensation.
(2) Commercial fleet vehicle means any motor vehicle owned, leased, controlled, dispatched, managed, or operated as part of a business or commercial service for the transportation of passengers for compensation, whether such compensation is paid directly for the transportation or as part of another service. The term includes vehicles utilized in taxicab, transportation network, rideshare, shuttle, autonomous transportation, or similar passenger transportation services, regardless of whether the vehicle is operated by a human driver, remotely operated, or operated by an automated driving system.
(3) Commercial fleet staging means the parking, standing, queuing, waiting, or idling of a commercial fleet vehicle while such vehicle is available for, awaiting, repositioning for, or anticipating a future passenger trip, assignment, or dispatch and is not actively engaged in the immediate pickup or drop-off of a passenger.
(4) Designated community area means a public park, cemetery, recreational facility, or other public property or public right-of-way designated by the mayor and council pursuant to subsection (d) of this section.
(5) Residential street means any public street or portion thereof within the city that is located within or primarily serves an area zoned for residential use.
(c) Commercial fleet staging prohibited.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any commercial fleet operator to cause, permit, direct, dispatch, or otherwise allow a commercial fleet vehicle to engage in commercial fleet staging on a residential street or within a designated community area.
(2) The prohibition established by this section shall apply regardless of whether the commercial fleet vehicle is operated by a human driver, remotely operated, or operated by an automated driving system.
(3) Nothing in this section shall prohibit a commercial fleet vehicle from:
a. Traveling upon a residential street or through a designated community area in accordance with applicable law;
b. Stopping for such time as is reasonably necessary for the immediate pickup or drop-off of a passenger;
c. Stopping when required by traffic conditions, a traffic-control device, the direction of a law enforcement officer, or an emergency;
d. Stopping because of a mechanical failure, collision, safety condition, or other circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the commercial fleet operator or vehicle; or
e. Lawfully parking at a location for a purpose unrelated to commercial fleet staging.
(d) Designation of additional community areas. The city council may, by resolution, designate city-owned or city-controlled public parks, cemeteries, recreational facilities, public parking areas, public rights-of-way, or other public property or community areas within the city in which commercial fleet staging shall be prohibited. In making such designation, the city council may consider traffic and parking conditions, pedestrian activity, surrounding land uses, public safety, documented instances of commercial fleet staging, impacts upon surrounding neighborhoods or community facilities, and such other factors as the city council deems relevant to the public health, safety, and welfare.
(e) Enforcement and penalties. Any person or commercial fleet operator violating this section shall be subject to the penalties provided in section 1-8 of this Code. Each vehicle and each separate occurrence of commercial fleet staging in violation of this section shall constitute a separate offense.
(f) Construction. This section regulates the parking, standing, staging, queuing, waiting, and idling of commercial fleet vehicles and shall not be construed to prohibit or otherwise regulate the lawful operation of an autonomous vehicle or automated driving system authorized by applicable state law.
(Ord. No. 2026-21, § 1, 9-21-26)

1788:
(a) The followings words, terms and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Cleared (as applied to taximeters) means a taximeter is inoperative with respect to all fare indication, when no indication of fare or extras is shown and when all parts are in those positions in which they are designed to be when the vehicle on which the taximeter is installed is not engaged by a passenger.
Face (as applied to taximeters) means that side of a taximeter upon which passenger charges are indicated.
Multiple-tariff taximeter means a taximeter that may be set to calculate fares at any one of two (2) or more rates.
Road test means a distance test, over a measured course, of a complete taximeter assembly when installed on a vehicle, the mechanism being actuated as a result of vehicle travel.
Single-tariff taximeter means a taximeter that calculates fares at a single rate only.
(b) Effective July 1, 2016, all taxicabs, shall be operated with taximeters, and all such taximeters shall be utilized for every passenger trip. If and when so equipped, the taximeters shall be made available to the passengers thereof at all times, day and night. The taximeter shall conform to the requirements of this section.
(c) Taxicabs providing taxicab services shall be subject to two (2) random inspections of taximeters per calendar year. The following will be inspected:
Taximeter inspection criteria. All taxicabs shall comply with the following at all times, and all random inspections shall be conducted by the department at a designated location and time and shall consist of the following inspection:
a. Design of indicating elements.
i. Generally. A taximeter shall be equipped with a primary indicating element.
ii. Advancement of indicating elements. Except when a taximeter is being cleared, the primary indicating elements shall be susceptible of advancement only by the rotation of the vehicle wheels or by the time mechanism.
iii. Visibility of indications. Except when a taximeter is being cleared, indications of fare and extras shall be clearly shown on its face at all times and at least ten (10) millimeter high for the fare and four (4) millimeter high for all other indications.
iv. Actuation of fare-indicating mechanism. When a taximeter designed to calculate fares upon the basis of a combination of distance traveled and time elapsed is operative with respect to fare indication, the fare-indicating mechanism shall be actuated by the distance mechanism whenever the vehicle is in motion at such a speed that the rate of distance revenue equals or exceeds the time rate and may be actuated by the time mechanism whenever the vehicle speed is less than this and when the vehicle is not in motion. Means shall be provided for the vehicle operator to render the time mechanism either operative or inoperative with respect to the fare-indicating mechanism.
b. Operating condition.
i. Generally. Whenever the indicating elements of a taximeter are set to indicate a charge for the hire of the vehicle, the character of the fare indication shall be clearly shown on the taximeter face. When a taximeter is cleared, the indication "not registering," "vacant" or an equivalent expression shall be shown.
ii. Single-tariff taximeter. Whenever a single-tariff taximeter is set so as to register charges, the indication "registering," "hired" or an equivalent expression shall be shown on the taximeter face.
iii. Multiple-tariff taximeter. Whenever a multiple-tariff taximeter is set so as to register charges, the basis for the particular tariff for which it is set shall be shown on the taximeter face.
iv. Extra charges. Extra charges shall be indicated as a separate item and shall not be included in the fare indication. They shall be identified by the term "extras" or by an equivalent expression. Values shall be defined by suitable words or monetary signs.
v. Protection of indications. Indications of fare and extras shall be displayed on the taximeter face through and entirely protected by glass or other suitable transparent material securely attached to the housing of the taximeter.
vi. Basis of fare calculations. A taximeter shall calculate fares only upon the basis of distance traveled, time elapsed or a combination of distance traveled and time elapsed.
c. Design of operating control.
i. Means of control. A control lever-arm knob, handle or other convenient and effective means shall be provided to set the taximeter mechanism for the desired operating condition and to clear the taximeter.
ii. Positions of control. The several positions of the control lever shall be mechanically defined, and displacement from any of these positions shall be sufficiently obstructed that the accidental or inadvertent changing of the operating condition of the taximeter is improbable. Possible movement of this control to an operating position immediately following its movement to the cleared position shall automatically be delayed enough to permit the taximeter mechanism to come to complete rest in the cleared condition.
d. Provision for security seals. Adequate provision shall be made for affixing lead-and-wire seals to a taximeter and to other parts required for service operation of a complete installation on a vehicle so that no adjustments, alterations or replacements affecting in any way the accuracy or indications of the device or the assembly can be made without mutilating the seals. The sealing means shall be such that it is not necessary to disassemble or remove any part of the device or of the vehicle to apply or inspect the seals.
e. Distance test methods. To determine compliance with distance tolerances, a distance test of a taximeter shall be conducted utilizing a road test.
f. Tolerance values.
i. Distance tests. Maintenance and acceptance tolerances for taximeters shall be as follows:
A. On overregistration, one percent of the interval under test.
B. On underregistration, four percent of the interval under test, with an added tolerance of one hundred (100) feet or thirty (30) miles whenever the initial interval is included in the interval under test.
ii. Time tests on individual time intervals. Maintenance and acceptance tolerances on individual time intervals shall be as follows:
A. On overregistration, three (3) seconds per minute (five (5) percent).
B. On underregistration, nine (9) seconds per minute (fifteen (15) percent) on the initial interval and six (6) seconds per minute (ten (10) percent) on subsequent intervals.
g. Time mechanism tests. The time mechanism shall be tested at least through the first five (5) time intervals.
h. User requirements.
i. Position and illumination of taximeter. When mounted upon a vehicle, a taximeter shall be so located that its face can be seen by a passenger from the rear compartment of the vehicle. Adequate lighting facilities shall be provided for so illuminating the face of the taximeter that the indications thereof may be conveniently read by the passenger, and the face of the taximeter shall be so illuminated whenever the taximeter is in operation and artificial illumination is necessary for the convenient reading of its indications.
ii. Statement of rates. The distance and time rates for which a taximeter is adjusted shall be given.
(d) The regulatory fee shall encompass the fee(s) for inspections performed under this chapter.
(e) Taxicabs will be identified by their vehicle identification numbers (VIN) for purposes of inspections.
(f) At least seventy-two (72) hours prior to the date of inspection, the provider will be contacted by the department by certified mail, return receipt requested, at its last known address, and informed that a certain taxicab's inspection is to be performed at a certain date, time and location. Notwithstanding subsection (d) of this section, should such taxicab fail to appear at the designated location at the designated date, time and location, the provider and/or the driver of such taxicab is subject to a no-show fee of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00).
(g) Should a taxicab fail any inspection, the taxicab shall be subject to random bi-weekly inspections until compliance is achieved. Notwithstanding subsection (d) of this section, the provider and/or driver of such taxicab shall pay a fee of fifty dollars ($50.00) per bi-weekly inspection under this subsection.
(h) Nothing in this article shall prohibit any inspections, in addition to those required under subsection (c) above, of a taxicab based upon the reasonable suspicion of violations under this section by a police officer of the department. Such inspections under this subsection are not subject to a fee.
(Ord. No. 2016-15, § 1(Exh. A), 5-2-16)

(a) Secondhand dealer means any individual, corporation, business, partnership or entity who, exclusively or as incidental to or in connection with other business, purchases, sells or acquires in trade or consignment used or secondhand goods, as defined below:
(1) Secondhand goods shall include but not be limited to electronics of any kind or description, video games, jewelry of any kind or description, watches and clocks or articles of that kind or description made in whole or in part of gold, silver, platinum or other precious or semiprecious metals; diamonds, emeralds, rubies or other precious or semiprecious stones; pistols or guns; bicycles or bicycle accessories; tools; office equipment; military service medals; or sporting goods, equipment, or accessories, shall, for the purpose of this article, be a secondhand dealer.

(2) A trustee in bankruptcy, executor, administrator, or receiver who has presented proof of such status to the secondhand dealer.
(3) A sale on the execution, or by virtue of any process issued by a court, if proof thereof has been presented to the secondhand dealer. The secondhand dealer shall keep such proof for two (2) years.

1807:
(a) Engaging in the business of buying or accepting in barter or trade used or previously owned goods within the incorporated areas of College Park is hereby declared to affect the public interest due to the opportunity it affords for the disposal of stolen property.
(b) In the public interest and as set forth herein, all secondhand dealers shall maintain records in sequential order by transaction number documenting all secondhand transactions as set forth herein.
(1) All secondhand dealers shall document an accurate description of each article of property sold, bartered, or traded to the secondhand dealer. Such description shall include, to the extent possible, the manufacturer, model, serial number, style, material, kind, color, design, number of stones if jewelry, and all other identifying names, marks, and numbers. The secondhand dealer shall assign a sequential transaction number which shall follow the previous transaction number one by one with no numbers skipped or omitted, documenting each transaction, and ensure each item received is tagged with the transaction number.
(2) A well-focused, properly exposed, color digital photograph of each article sold, bartered or traded to the secondhand dealer shall be made at the time of acquisition of any article, and of each article's serial number if imprinted on the article, which number shall be clearly visible and readable in the images. If the article was never imprinted with any type of serial number, then the image shall show the entire article. All such digital images shall be labeled with the transaction number and stored in such a manner that they are safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review.
(3) The tag bearing the transaction number must be created and remain attached to the item until the property is disposed of by sale, trade, or other lawful means. This subsection does not apply to the purchase of property from licensed wholesale or distributor businesses for the purpose of retail sales; however the secondhand dealer shall be required to maintain all purchasing records for property exempted from this subsection.
(4) All secondhand dealers shall require all persons selling, bartering, or trading property to show proper identification prior to conducting a secondhand dealer transaction. Proper identification is defined as a government issued photo identification card such as a driver's license, military identification card, state identification card, or passport.
(5) All secondhand dealers shall also document the name, address, telephone number, race, sex, height, weight, drivers' license or other government identification number, date of birth, and Social Security Number of the person selling, bartering, or trading the property, along with the date and time of the transaction. This documentation shall be made at the time of the transaction and labeled with the transaction number.
(6) All secondhand dealers shall take a well-focused, properly exposed, color digital photograph of the person selling, bartering, or trading the property. The photograph shall clearly show a frontal view of the subject's face along with the broker's ticket transaction number. Digital images shall be labeled with the transaction number and stored in such a manner that they are safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review by law enforcement personnel. Such images shall be stored for a minimum period of four (4) years from the date of creation.
(7) All secondhand dealers shall obtain from each person selling, bartering, or trading any property, the fingerprint (using an electronic digital fingerprint scanner) of the right hand index finger, unless such finger is missing, in which event the print of the next finger in existence on the right hand shall be obtained with a notation as to the exact finger printed. The fingerprint shall be imprinted onto the transaction form in the designated area along with the signature of the person selling, bartering, or trading the property. The fingerprint must be clear and legible. In the event that more than one transaction form is required, a fingerprint and signature shall be obtained for each form. Fingerprints and the information required herein shall be obtained each time such person sells, barters, or trades any property.
(8) Items of property that appear to be new, unused, and in their original packaging cannot be accepted by the secondhand dealer unless the customer can supply a copy of the original sales receipt, or other proof of purchase from the place of purchase, to the secondhand dealer who shall retain the receipt or proof of purchase on file, labeled with the transaction number.
(9) All secondhand dealers shall store the above documentation, digital images, and digital fingerprints, which shall comprise the record of each transaction, together by the transaction number and shall maintain said records for a period of four (4) years and make them available to law enforcement personnel upon request. Both a hard copy and an electronic copy of these stored records shall be kept on-site, which must be kept safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review, may, if otherwise permitted by law, serve as the permanent record of the secondhand dealer.
(10) All secondhand dealers shall enter the complete record of each transaction as it occurs into the electronic automated reporting system via the internet to the administrator of the electronic automated reporting system. The administrator of the electronic automated reporting system will electronically transmit all transactions to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)

1809:
(a) All secondary dealers shall make a daily report, in such form as may be prescribed by the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority, of all secondary dealer transactions that occurred during the previous twenty-four (24) hours ending at 7:00 p.m. on the date of the report.
(b) Daily reports shall include all information as required by section 21-28(b).
(c) All secondary dealers shall enter each transaction as it occurs into the designated electronic automated reporting system via the internet to the administrator of the electronic automated reporting system. The administrator of the electronic automated reporting system will electronically transmit all transactions to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority.

In this event, the secondary dealers will be required to make records of transactions on paper forms. A digital camera will be used to collect the required pictures, which are to be transferred to a CD for submittal. The paper forms must include all information as enumerated in section 21-28(b). Secondary dealers shall maintain a minimum three (3) day supply of these paper forms. (a) Definition. For the purpose of this section, a watch shall be deemed to be secondhand if:
(1) It, as a whole, or the case thereof or the movement thereof has been previously sold to or acquired by any person for such person's use or the use of another, but not for resale; provided, however, a watch that has been so sold or acquired and is thereafter returned either through exchange or for credit to the original vendor who sold or passed title to the watch shall not be deemed to be a secondhand watch for the purpose of this section, if the vendor shall keep a written or printed record setting forth the name of the purchaser thereof, the date of the sale or transfer thereof and the serial number, if any, on the case and movement and any other distinguishing number or identification mark, which record shall be kept five (5) years from the date of the sale or transfer and shall be open for inspection during all business hours by the law enforcement or regulatory inspectors;
(2) Its case or movement of serial numbers or other distinguishing numbers or identification marks shall be erased, defaced, removed, altered or covered; or
(3) Its movement is more than five (5) years old and has been repaired by any person, including the vendor, notwithstanding that it may have been returned either through exchange or for credit to the original vendor. Cleaning and oiling a watch movement or recasing the movement in a new case shall not be deemed a watch repair for the purpose of this subsection.
(b) Tagging. Any person engaged in the business of buying or selling watches, who may sell or exchange or offer for sale or exchange, expose for sale or exchange, possess with the intent to sell or exchange or display with the intent to sell or exchange any secondhand watch shall affix and keep affixed thereto a tag with the term "secondhand" clearly and legibly written or printed thereon, which shall be affixed or placed so that the term "secondhand" shall be plainly visible at all times.
(c) Contents of invoice; records. Any person who may sell a secondhand watch or in any other way pass title thereto shall deliver to the vendee a written invoice bearing the term "secondhand" in bold letters larger than any other written matter upon the invoice. The invoice shall further set forth the name and address of the vendor, the name and address of the vendee, the date of the sale, the name of the watch or its maker and the serial number, if any, and any other distinguishing numbers or identification marks upon its case and movement. If the serial number or other distinguishing numbers or identification marks shall have been erased, defaced, removed, altered or covered, the invoice shall so state. The vendor shall keep on file a duplicate of the invoice five (5) years from the sale thereof, which shall be open to inspection during all business hours by the law enforcement or regulatory inspectors.
(d) Advertising. Any person who may advertise or display in any manner a secondhand watch for sale or exchange shall state clearly in the advertisement or display that the watch is secondhand.

1818:
(a) Initiation and service of the petition.
(1) The petitioner shall file a petition with the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority which shall appoint a hearing officer that shall determine ownership of the property within forty-five (45) days of the conclusion of the criminal investigation or criminal proceedings involving the property. Such petition shall set forth the following:
a. The facts establishing compliance with section 21-38;
b. The name and address of each person described in section 21-38(d); and
c. An accurate description of the property, any identifying marks or serial numbers, the police identification number(s), the location where the property is currently being held, and the person from whom seized, if the property was in fact seized.
(2) The petition shall be served by personal service or by first class mail, postage prepaid, return receipt requested, upon all persons known to have an interest in the property, each person described and named in section 21-38(d), in all cases, the person from whom the property was obtained or who currently possesses the property subject to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority hold.
(3) A copy of sections 21-37 through 21-40 of this article shall be served with each petition.
(b) Hearing.
(1) Notice.
a. There shall be served with the petition a notice of hearing setting forth the date, time and place for the conduct of the hearing to determine the right of possession to the property. The hearing date shall not be sooner than twenty-five (25), nor more than forty-five (45), calendar days after the date of service of the petition and notice.
b. Service shall be made to the last known address of all persons included in subsection (b) of this section.
c. Service shall be complete upon receipt. If service is made by certified mail, the return receipt shall be prima facie evidence of service.
d. Proof of service upon each potential claimant shall be delivered to the hearing officer.
(2) Hearing officers.
a. The secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority shall have the authority to appoint a hearing officer for the purpose of acting as a fact finder regarding disputes of ownership of property brought by a petitioner. The hearing officer shall be appointed for a two (2) year term and shall receive seventy-five dollars ($75.00) for each day or part thereof the hearing officer appears for such hearings. The hearing officer shall be a licensed attorney at law with at least three (3) years' experience in the practice of law. No person shall be appointed as a hearing officer who holds any interest in any licenses issued under the police powers of the city or who represents any interest which may be adverse to that of the city.
(3) Conduct.
a. The hearing shall be conducted informally by a hearing officer and the technical rules of evidence shall not apply, provided that the decision of the hearing officer shall in all cases be based upon substantial and reliable evidence. All parties shall have the right to be represented by counsel, to present evidence and testimony in support of their position, and to cross-examine adverse witnesses. All witnesses shall be placed under oath before testifying.
b. The burden of proof in determining property ownership shall be by a preponderance of the evidence, and shall at all times be upon the person or persons challenging the possession of the party from whom the property was taken by law enforcement, even if the party from whom the property was taken does not appear at the hearing. If the property was not seized by law enforcement, the burden of proof shall at all times be upon the person or persons challenging the party who currently possesses the property subject to the hold.
c. The hearing shall be recorded electronically or by other means.
d. The decision of the hearing officer shall be issued within ten (10) calendar days of the close of the record. The decision shall be in writing, and shall be mailed postage prepaid to each respondent or claimant appearing. A copy of the decision shall also be sent to the respective law enforcement agencies.
e. The decision of the hearing officer shall be final upon issuance.

(a) Each applicant seeking a license to operate as a secondhand dealer shall submit an application to the police department containing the following information:

Upon completion of the criminal investigation report, the police department shall assemble the tendered application forms and accompanying documents relating to investigation and processing of the application and deliver such documents to the city clerk. If the criminal investigation report shows that the applicant fails to meet the requirements set by this article, or if the applicant fails to meet all other requirements outlined by this article, then the city clerk shall inform the applicant, in writing, that the application has been denied. If the application is denied, such written notification shall set forth in reasonable detail the reasons for the denial and shall notify the applicant of his right to appeal. (i) In all instances in which an application is denied, the applicant may not reapply for the same type of license for at least one year from the date of denial.

1835:
(a) Engaging in the business of buying or accepting in pledge, pawn, exchange, barter or trade used or previously owned goods within the incorporated areas of College Park is hereby declared to affect the public interest due to the opportunity it affords for the disposal of stolen property.
(b) In the public interest and as set forth herein, all pawnbrokers shall maintain records in sequential order by transaction number documenting all pawn transactions as set forth herein.
(1) All pawnbrokers shall document an accurate description of each article of property pledged, pawned, exchanged, bartered, traded, or sold to the pawnbroker. Such description shall include, to the extent possible, the manufacturer, model, serial number, style, material, kind, color, design, number of stones if jewelry, and all other identifying names, marks, and numbers. The pawnbroker shall assign a sequential transaction number which shall follow the previous transaction number one by one with no numbers skipped or omitted, documenting each transaction, and ensure each item received is tagged with the pawnshop transaction number.
(2) A well-focused, properly exposed, color digital photograph of each article pledged, pawned, exchanged, bartered, traded, or sold to the pawnbroker shall be made at the time of acquisition of any article and of each article's serial number, which number shall be clearly visible and readable in the images if imprinted on the article. If the article was never imprinted with any type of serial number, then the image shall show the entire article. All such digital images shall be labeled with the transaction number and stored in such a manner that they are safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review.
(3) The tag bearing the pawnshop transaction number must be created and remain attached to the item until the property is disposed of by sale, trade, or other lawful means. This paragraph does not apply to the purchase of property from licensed wholesale or distributor businesses for the purpose of retail sales; however the pawnbroker shall be required to maintain all purchasing records for property exempted from this paragraph.
(4) The pawnbroker shall require all persons pledging, pawning, exchanging, bartering, trading, or selling property to show proper identification prior to conducting a pawnshop transaction. Proper identification is defined as a government-issued photo identification card such as a driver's license, military identification card, state identification card, or passport.
(5) The pawnbroker shall also document the name, address, telephone number, race, sex, height, weight, driver's license or other government identification number, date of birth, and social security number of the person pledging, pawning, exchanging, bartering, trading, or selling the property, along with the date and time of the transaction. This documentation shall be made at the time of the transaction and labeled with the transaction number.
(6) At the time of acquisition of the property by the pawnbroker, the pawnbroker shall make and store a well-focused, properly exposed, digital photograph of the person pledging, pawning, exchanging, bartering, trading, or selling the property. The photograph shall clearly show a frontal view of the subject's face along with the pawnbroker's ticket transaction number. Digital images shall be labeled with the transaction number and stored in such a manner that they are safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review by law enforcement personnel. Such images shall be stored for a minimum period of four (4) years from the date of creation.
(7) The pawnbroker shall obtain from each person pledging, pawning, exchanging, bartering, trading, or selling any property, the fingerprint (using an electronic digital fingerprint scanner) of the right hand index finger, unless such finger is missing, in which event the print of the next finger in existence on the right hand shall be obtained with a notation as to the exact finger printed. The fingerprint shall be imprinted onto the pawn transaction form in the designated area along with the signature of the person pledging, pawning, exchanging, bartering, trading, or selling the property. The fingerprint must be clear and legible. In the event that more than one pawn transaction form is required, a fingerprint and signature shall be obtained for each form. Fingerprints and the information required herein shall be obtained each time such person pledges, pawns, exchanges, barters, trades, or sells any property.
(8) Items of property that appear to be new, unused, and in their original packaging cannot be accepted by the pawnbroker unless the customer can supply a copy of the original sales receipt, or other proof of purchase from the place of purchase, to the pawnbroker who shall retain the receipt or proof of purchase on file, labeled with the transaction number.
(9) The pawnbroker shall store the above documentation, digital images, and digital fingerprints, which shall comprise the record of each transaction, together by the transaction number and shall maintain said records for a period of four (4) years and make them available to law enforcement personnel upon request. Both a hard copy and an electronic copy of these stored records shall be kept on-site, which must be kept safe from corruption, readily identifiable, and readily available for review, may, if otherwise permitted by law, serve as the permanent record of the pawnbroker.
(10) All pawnbrokers shall enter the complete record of each transaction as it occurs into the electronic automated reporting system via the internet to the administrator of the electronic automated reporting system. The administrator of the electronic automated reporting system will electronically transmit all transactions to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority, as defined in section 21-69.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)

(a) All pawnbrokers shall make a daily report, in such form as may be prescribed by the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority, of all pawnshop transactions that occurred during the previous twenty-four (24) hours ending at 7:00 p.m. on the date of the report.

The following terms used in this article shall have the meanings indicated below:
Accepted identification means an official document, most commonly in the form of a plastic coated/sealed card, issued for purposes of identification or driver's license. These documents must be issued by one of the fifty (50) states or a branch of the U.S. Military, i.e., Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines, Coast Guard, or current State of Georgia and counties of Georgia probation and parole cards. The identification must, at a minimum, bear a true photograph of the person presenting it, date of birth, description of the person, and an address for the person.
City means the City of College Park, Georgia.
Deceptive business practice means:
(1) Any use or possession of a false weight or measurement, or any other device for falsely determining or recording any quality or quantity in connection with any scale or service;
(2) Any sale of, offer to sell or delivery of less than the represented quality or quantity;
(3) Any attempt to take more than the represented quantity of any commodity, when as buyer or broker, he or she furnishes the weight or measure;
(4) Any service which is of an unreasonably lesser quality than the service offered or represented;
(5) Any other practice designated as unlawful by O.C.G.A. § 10-1-390 et seq.; or
(6) Any other fraudulent business transaction which is made punishable by the laws of the State of Georgia.
Good moral character means a person who has not been convicted of any felony or any crime involving theft, fraud or a crime against property in the past ten (10) years.
Interest in a pawnshop exists if the person involved or any member of his or her immediate family is the outright owner of the pawnshop; a co-owner of the pawnshop; a partner in a partnership which owns all or part of the pawnshop; a stockholder in any corporation organized for pecuniary gain which owns all or any part of the pawnshop.
License means permission to operate a pawnshop pursuant to grant by the city council. May also be referred to as a pawnshop license.
Minor means any person who has not attained the age of 18 years.
New in box means any unused item in the original unopened, factory sealed boxes.
Pawn or pledge means a bailment, or personal property or title (including but not limited to a motor vehicle title) as security for any debt or engagement, redeemable upon certain terms and with the express or implied power of sale on default.
Pawnbroker means any person engaged in whole or in part in the business of lending money on the security of pledged goods, personal property or titles, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property or title on the condition that it may be redeemed or repurchased by the seller for a fixed price within a fixed period of time, or in the business of purchasing tangible personal property or title from persons or sources other than the manufacturers or regulated dealers as a part of or in conjunction with the business activities described herein.
Pawnshop means any business wherein a well-defined part thereof is to take or receive, by way of pledge, pawn or exchange, any goods, wares, merchandise, motor vehicles, or any kind of personal property or title whatsoever, as security for the repayment of money lent thereon.
Permit means permission to be employed or work in a pawnshop regulated by the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority.
Person means the term shall extend and be applied to associations, firms, partnerships and bodies politic and corporate, or any combination thereof, as well as to individuals.
Police department means the City of College Park Chief of Police or his or her designee.
Secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority means the chief of police or his or her designee until such time as a multi-jurisdictional operation regulating and monitoring secondhand dealers, pawn brokers, precious metals dealers, secondary metal recyclers, and like dealers is in place. Once a multi-jurisdictional regulatory and monitoring operation is in place, the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority shall mean that multi-jurisdictional operation.

(a) Initiation and service of the petition.
(1) The petitioner shall file a petition with the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority which shall appoint a hearing officer that shall determine ownership of the property within forty-five (45) days of the conclusion of the criminal investigation or criminal proceedings involving the property. Such petition shall set forth the following:
a. The facts establishing compliance with section 21-72;
b. The name and address of each person described in section 21-72(d); and
c. An accurate description of the property, any identifying marks or serial numbers, the police identification number(s), the location where the property is currently being held, and the person from whom seized, if the property was in fact seized.
(2) The petition shall be served by personal service or by first class mail, postage prepaid, return receipt requested, upon all persons known to have an interest in the property, each person described and named in section 21-72(d), in all cases, the person from whom the property was obtained or who currently possesses the property subject to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority hold.
(3) A copy of sections 21-71 through 21-74 of this article shall be served with each petition.
(b) Hearing.
(1) Notice.
a. There shall be served with the petition a notice of hearing setting forth the date, time and place for the conduct of the hearing to determine the right of possession to the property. The hearing date shall not be sooner than twenty-five (25), nor more than forty-five (45), calendar days after the date of service of the petition and notice.
b. Service shall be made to the last known address of all persons included in subsection (b) of this section.
c. Service shall be complete upon receipt. If service is made by certified mail, the return receipt shall be prima facie evidence of service.
d. Proof of service upon each potential claimant shall be delivered to the hearing officer.
(2) Hearing officers.
a. The secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority shall have the authority to appoint a hearing officer for the purpose of acting as a fact finder regarding disputes of ownership of property brought by a petitioner. The hearing officer shall be appointed for a two (2) year term and shall receive seventy-five dollars ($75.00) for each day or part thereof the hearing officer appears for such hearings. The hearing officer shall be a licensed attorney at law with at least three (3) years' experience in the practice of law. No person shall be appointed as a hearing officer who holds any interest in any licenses issued under the police powers of the city or who represents any interest which may be adverse to that of the city.
(3) Conduct.
a. The hearing shall be conducted informally by a hearing officer and the technical rules of evidence shall not apply, provided that the decision of the hearing officer shall in all cases be based upon substantial and reliable evidence. All parties shall have the right to be represented by counsel, to present evidence and testimony in support of their position, and to cross-examine adverse witnesses. All witnesses shall be placed under oath before testifying.
b. The burden of proof in determining property ownership shall be by a preponderance of the evidence, and shall at all times be upon the person or persons challenging the possession of the party from whom the property was taken by law enforcement, even if the party from whom the property was taken does not appear at the hearing. If the property was not seized by law enforcement, the burden of proof shall at all times be upon the person or persons challenging the party who currently possesses the property subject to the hold.
c. The hearing shall be recorded electronically or by other means.
d. The decision of the hearing officer shall be issued within ten (10) calendar days of the close of the record. The decision shall be in writing, and shall be mailed postage prepaid to each respondent or claimant appearing. A copy of the decision shall also be sent to the respective law enforcement agencies.
e. The decision of the hearing officer shall be final upon issuance.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)

1851:
(a) It is unlawful for any person to engage in, conduct or carry on within the city any pawnshop, as defined in this article, without a pawnshop license. A proper application for renewal within the time required must be submitted and such license shall not be under suspension or permanently or conditionally revoked.
(b) Every person, before engaging in, conducting or carrying on with the city any pawnshop, shall first file an application with the police department for a license to operate a pawnshop. The application shall be made on an annual basis. No license shall be issued until a fee in an amount established by action of the city council, a copy of which is on file in the office of the city clerk, is paid to the city.
(c) The chief of police or any other official of the city designated by the city council, shall investigate each applicant for a license under this article and determine whether such applicant is a person of good character and has not been convicted of a criminal offense as indicated in this article.
(d) The annual fee for each license to operate a pawnshop and each pawnshop employee permit shall be set forth by resolution of the city council and may be set in a fee schedule of the city. In addition, each pawnshop shall be subject to the business and occupation taxes outlined in article I of chapter 11 of the Code.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)
1852:
Any pawnshop operated, conducted or maintained contrary to the provisions of this article shall be declared to be unlawful and a public nuisance. The city may, in addition to, or in lieu of prosecuting a criminal violation hereunder, commence an action or actions, proceeding or proceedings for abatement, removal or enjoinment thereof, in the manner provided by law. It shall take such other steps and shall apply to such court or courts as may have jurisdiction to grant such relief as will abate or remove such pawnshop and restrain and enjoin any person from operating, conducting or maintaining a pawnshop contrary to the provisions of this chapter. In addition, violation of the provisions of this article shall be per se grounds for suspension or revocation of any related permit or license granted hereunder.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)
1853:
(a) Each applicant seeking a license to operate a pawnshop shall submit an application to the police department containing the following information:
(1) The full name, age, street address, mailing address, phone number, facsimile number, e-mail address, Social Security number, and date of birth of the applicant.
(2) The name and physical address of the proposed business.
(3) The nature and character of the business.
(4) If the applicant is a partnership, the name of the partnership and the full names and mailing addresses of the partners.
(5) If the applicant is a corporation, the name of the corporation and the full names and mailing addresses of its officers, the members of its board of directors and its principal stockholders.
(6) Any bank accounts listed in the name of the applicant, or maintained by the applicant, whether an individual, partnership or corporation.
(7) Whether the applicant, or any partners, or any corporation officers or board members, or principal shareholders, has been convicted by the federal government, any state, or any city in the United States of any felony, any crime involving theft, fraud, or against property, or any violation of the "Family Violence Act." "Conviction" as used in this section shall include an adjudication of guilt, a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, or the forfeiture of a bond.
(8) A listing of all real property which the applicant, partnership, or corporation is presently leasing, and the names and addresses of all lessees and lessors of such property.
(9) A certified copy of the applicant's financial statement for the twelve-month period ending one week before the filing of the application for license, and state of incorporation of such corporation, as well as the names and addresses of the agents and employees of such corporation for a period of two years immediately prior to the filing of such application.
(b) The police chief or any other official of the city designated by the city council shall establish a form by which an application under this section is to be made and shall make copies of the form available to the public upon request. An applicant seeking to obtain a license under this section shall submit the application by completing the provided form.
(c) All applications shall be completed by the applicant and sworn to and signed by the applicant in the presence of a notary public or other officer authorized to administer oaths.
(d) Each applicant shall certify on the application that they have read this article and, if the license is granted, each licensee shall maintain a copy of this article on the premises.
(e) Each applicant shall complete a waiver in order for a record of the applicant's criminal history to be obtained.
(f) All applicants shall furnish all data, information and records requested of them by the city council, the police department or other official designated by the city council, and failure to furnish such data, information, and records within thirty (30) days from the date of such request shall automatically serve as grounds to deny the application. An applicant, by filing an application, agrees to produce for questioning any person(s) who are considered relevant to the ascertainment of facts relative to such license, as may be requested by the city council, the police department, or other official designated by the city council. The failure to produce such persons within thirty (30) days after being requested to do so may result in denial of the application.
(g) Once an application, accompanying documents, and the required license fees are filed with the police department, the police department shall conduct a criminal investigation of the applicant and prepare a written criminal investigation report detailing all information relating to fingerprinting, criminal history, arrest data, and other matters pertinent to law enforcement. Upon completion of the criminal investigation report, the police department shall assemble the tendered application forms and accompanying documents relating to investigation and processing of the application and deliver such documents to the city clerk. If the criminal investigation report shows that the applicant fails to meet the requirements set by this article, or if the applicant fails to meet all other requirements outlined by this article, then the city clerk shall inform the applicant, in writing, that the application has been denied. The written notification shall set forth in reasonable detail the reasons for the denial and shall inform the applicant of his right to appeal. Such appeal shall be before the city council in accordance with section 21-91. If an applicant desires to appeal a denial, the applicant must file a written request for an appeal with the city clerk within ten (10) business days of the date of the written notice informing the applicant of the denial of the license.
(h) Any application for a license to operate a pawnshop that the city clerk determines satisfies all the requirements outlined in this article, including character requirements as contained in the criminal investigation report of the police department, shall be scheduled for review at the next regularly scheduled public meeting of the city council. At that meeting, the applicant and any person(s) opposed to such application have the right to present to the city council any information that the city council determines is relevant to the licensing decision. In making its determination on whether to approve or deny the application, the city council shall look to the qualifications set forth in this article and consider the public interest and welfare of the citizens of the city. The council shall have the discretion to grant or deny the application based on the information presented. A decision by the city council shall be made within thirty (30) days from the date of the public hearing, unless the decision is postponed for purposes of obtaining additional information deemed necessary for consideration of the application. Notice of the decision by the city council shall be mailed to the applicant. If the application is denied, such written notification shall set forth in reasonable detail the reasons for the denial and shall notify the applicant of his right to appeal. Such appeal shall be taken solely in accordance with section 21-91.
(i) In all instances in which an application is denied, the applicant may not reapply for the same type of license for at least one year from the date of denial.
(j) Upon the issuance of a license to operate a pawnshop, the licensee must have and continuously maintain in the city a registered agent upon whom any process, notice, or demand required or permitted by law or under this ordinance may be served. This agent must be an individual and must be a resident of city. The licensee shall submit the name of such agent, along with the written consent of such agent, to the city clerk. The identity of the agent may also be submitted contemporaneous to filing the license application.
(k) Upon approval by the city council of the application for a license, the city clerk shall issue a license in accordance with the approved application. If the applicant is an individual, the license shall be issued in the name of the individual. If the application is a corporation, the license shall be issued in the name of the corporation and in the name of the majority stockholder or a principal officer of the corporation. If the application is a partnership, the license shall be issued in the name of the partnership and in the name of one of the partners. All licenses issued shall be granted for the full calendar year or for the number of months remaining in the calendar year. Any applicant granted a license before July 1 shall pay the full license fee without proration. License fees for licenses granted on or after July 1 shall be one-half (½) the annual license fee. License fees are not refundable once the license is granted by the city.

1854:
Any person who desires to obtain a license to operate a pawnshop must meet the minimum qualifications set forth in this section. If the applicant is a partnership, each partner must meet the qualifications of any individual license and must make sworn statements of these qualifications as part of the application process. If the applicant is a corporation, each principal officer, each member of the board of directors, and each principal stockholder of the corporation must meet the qualifications as part of the application process.
(a) No license to operate a pawnshop or renewal license to operate such a business shall be issued to any applicant where any individual, having an interest either as owner, partner, officer, or principal shareholder, directly beneficial or absolute, has been convicted by the federal government, any state, or any city in the United States of any felony, any crime involving theft, fraud, or against property, or any violation of the "Family Violence Act." "Conviction" as used in this section shall include an adjudication of guilt, a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, or the forfeiture of a bond.
(b) No license shall be granted to an applicant who is less than eighteen (18) years of age.
(c) No pawnshop shall be operated at the same location or in the same premises as any secondhand dealership, any precious metals dealership, or any secondary metals recycler. No license for a pawnshop shall be issued for a location currently licensed as a secondhand dealership, as a precious metals dealership, or as a secondary metals recycler.
(d) No license shall be granted where the applicant has had any license, or any permit, to own or to operate a pawnshop, a secondhand dealership, a precious metals dealership, or a secondary metals recycler issued by any county, municipality, or other governmental subdivision suspended or revoked.
(e) No license to operate a pawnshop shall be issued if the application contains a material omission, untrue or misleading information, or if the application fails to indicate the true ownership of the proposed business.
(f) No license shall be issued where the applicant has failed to pay any required fee, including any fees or assessments owed to other departments of the city.
(g) No license shall be issued for a location that is not in compliance with any federal, state, or local regulation including, but not limited to, a state certificate of occupancy, a city certificate of occupancy, the zoning ordinances, or the fire code.
(h) There shall be issued only one license to operate a pawnshop for each ten thousand (10,000) population within the city as determined by the decennial census. In the event more than one qualified application is received at the same time for any available pawnbroker's license, the city shall conduct an unbiased lottery to determine which qualified application shall receive such license.
(i) No license shall be issued to a new applicant for a license to operate a pawnshop in a location which is within two thousand (2,000) feet of any existing licensed secondhand dealership, pawnshop, precious metals dealership, or secondary metal recycler.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)
1855:
(a) Any holder of a license to operate a pawnshop must, within six (6) months after the issuance of the license, open for business the establishment referred to in the license, unless such period is extended by the city clerk. Failure to open the licensed establishment as referred to in this subsection within the six (6) month period shall serve as an automatic forfeiture and cancellation of the license, and no refund of license fees shall be made to the license holder.
(b) Any holder of a license to operate a pawnshop who begins the operation of the business as authorized in the license and, for a period of three (3) consecutive months thereafter, ceases to operate the business as authorized in the license, shall automatically forfeit his license, which license shall, by virtue of such failure to operate, be canceled without the necessity for any further action by the city clerk or the city council.
(Ord. No. 2016-7, § 1(Exh. A), 2-15-16)
1856:
(a) The city council shall be authorized to suspend, revoke or place on probation with or without conditions, any license previously granted under the provisions of this article, upon hearing, with at least five (5) days' written notice mailed to the owner at the licensed establishment or upon one or more the following, as:
(1) An owner or holder of the license or permit gives false or misleading information in the original or renewal application for any license or permit required by this division.
(2) An owner commits a deceptive business practice as defined herein.
(3) An owner has knowingly allowed the continuous violation of an ordinance of the city or other law of the State of Georgia or federal law to occur on the premises.
(4) An owner has violated any provision of this article.
(5) An owner has been convicted of any felony or any crime involving theft, fraud or against property, by the State of Georgia or the city regarding an offense which was committed on the premises or which would otherwise violate the provisions of this article.
(6) An owner fails to pay any fee, occupation tax, fine, transaction fee or other amount of money due to the city under this article or any other ordinance of the city.
(7) An owner has failed to obtain, or has suffered the expiration, suspension or revocation of any paper or document necessary in pursuance of its business as may be required by any officer, agency, authority, or department of the city, state, or United States under authority of any law, ordinance or resolutions of the city, state or the United States.
(8) An owner made any misrepresentation of fact, whether through advertisement or through any form of direct communication oral or written, which is intended to mislead the public or to mislead any party with whom the owner deals in pursuance of the regulated business. The term misrepresentation of fact as used herein shall embrace not only express misrepresentations but also misrepresentations arising by virtue of the owner's conduct, including acts and omissions.
(9) An owner has failed to make an entry of any material matter in his or her permanent record; or falsified, obliterated, destroyed or removed from his or her place of business such permanent record.
(10) An owner has failed to submit the daily report to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority within the prescribed time; or has submitted an illegible, incomplete or improper daily report to the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority.
(11) An owner has refused to allow any duly authorized law enforcement officer to inspect his or her permanent record, his or her daily report or any goods in his or her possession during the ordinary hours of business or at any reasonable time.
(12) An owner has failed to maintain a record of each pawn transaction, and fingerprints and photographs for at least four (4) years.
(13) An owner has accepted a pledge or purchase of property from a person under the age of 18 years or who the owner knows is not the true owner of such property.
(14) An owner has made an agreement requiring the personal liability of the pledgor or seller or waiving any of the provisions of this part or providing for a maturity date less than one (1) month after the date of the pawn transaction.
(15) An owner has failed to return or replace the pledged goods to the pledgor or seller upon payment of the full amount due the owner unless the pledged goods have been taken into custody by a court or law enforcement officer or agency.
(16) An owner has failed to comply with any rules or regulations dealing with the implementation of this article by the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority.
(17) An owner has failed to adequately supervise and monitor the conduct of the employees, patrons, and others on the licensed premises, or on any property owned or leased by the licensee, including but not limited to the parking lots and parking areas, or on any parking lots or areas which may be lawfully used by patrons of the licensed establishment, in order to protect the safety and well being of the general public and of those utilizing the premises.
(18) Permitting the solicitation of patrons on the licensed premises for prostitution or any other illegal act where the owner, or the licensed establishment's employee or agent knew or should have known of such conduct.
(19) In the case of bankruptcy, receivership, or levy of legal process upon the licensed establishment or property therein.
(20) Except as provided in section 21-90, any change in the ownership of an entity owning a licensed outlet.
(21) The violation of any other law, ordinance, or regulation governing the operation of establishments licensed as pawnshops or which are reasonably related to the operation of such businesses.
(b) No permit which has been issued to any person pursuant to this division shall be suspended or revoked except upon one or more of the grounds stated in subsection (a) of this section and until after the holder of the permit has been afforded a hearing.
(c) No hearing as provided in subsection (b) of this section shall be held unless the holder of the permit has been given at least five (5) days written notice of the time, place and purpose of the hearing and a written statement of the charge upon which the hearing shall be held.
(d) Charges upon which any permit issues pursuant to this division may be initiated by the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority, the license and permit unit of the secondhand goods regulatory and monitoring authority or the city police department through formal citation.

1858:
(a) Qualifications. An employee of a pawnshop, as defined herein, shall not be less than eighteen (18) years of age. Every employee must be of good moral character as defined by this article. Any employee who has been convicted of any felony or crime involving theft, fraud or against property shall not be permitted to work on the premises of a pawnshop for a period of ten (10) years from the date of such conviction, unless a longer prohibition on such work is ordered by a court of competent jurisdiction. The term "on the premises" shall include all work done or services performed in the scope of employment elsewhere than on the regulated premises. "Conviction" as used in this section shall include an adjudication of guilt, a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, or the forfeiture of a bond.
(b) Approval for employment. Each applicant seeking a permit to work in a pawnshop shall submit an application to the police department containing the following information:
(1) The full name, age, street address, mailing address, phone number, facsimile number, e-mail address, Social Security number, and date of birth of the applicant.
(2) The name, physical address, mailing address, phone number, facsimile number, and e-mail address of the business where the applicant proposes to work.
(3) The nature and character of the business where the applicant proposes to work.
(4) If a partnership, the name of the partnership and the full names and mailing addresses of the partners.
(5) Whether the applicant has within the preceding ten (10) years, a record for any conviction for any felony or crime involving theft, fraud or against property.
(6) Any ownership or interest that the applicant has in any other pawnshop, whether it is sited locally or out-of-state, and the nature of such ownership or interest. An interest in a pawnshop shall have the meaning set forth in this article.
(c) The police chief or any other official of the city designated by the city council shall establish a form by which an application under this section is to be made and shall make copies of the form available to the public upon request. An applicant seeking to obtain a permit under this section shall submit the application by completing the provided form.
(d) All applications shall be completed by the applicant and sworn to and signed by the applicant in the presence of a notary public or other officer authorized to administer oaths.
(e) Each applicant shall certify on the application that they have read this article.
(f) Each applicant shall complete a waiver in order for the applicant's criminal history to be obtained.
(g) Each applicant must be fingerprinted by the police department at the time the application is filed.
(h) All applicants shall furnish all data, information and records requested of them by the city council, the police department or other official designated by the city council, and failure to furnish such data, information, and records within ten (10) days from the date of such request shall automatically serve as grounds to deny the application. An applicant, by filing an application, agrees to produce for questioning any person(s) who are considered relevant to the ascertainment of facts relative to such license, as may be requested by the city council, the police department, or other official designated by the city council. The failure to produce such persons within ten (10) days after being requested to do so may result in denial of the application.
(i) Independent contractors. For purposes of this article, the description of an employee or worker in a pawnshop or pawnbroker establishment as an independent contractor shall not exempt that employee or worker from obtaining a license for such employment.
(j) Once an application, accompanying documents, any other requested information, and the required investigative and license fees are filed, the city shall have ten (10) days to investigate the information submitted by the applicant. If the employee is found to be of good moral character, the police department shall grant an approval of employment and shall issue an annual personal identification card authorizing the person to be employed by a pawnshop. Upon approval the employee may begin working on the regulated premises. It shall be the duty of the pawnbroker to insure that the provisions of this section receive compliance. The employee is required to notify the police department of any change in information or circumstances which has occurred since the original approval was granted. If approval is denied, the applicant may, within ten (10) days, apply in writing to the police department for reconsideration setting forth in detail the reasons why reconsideration is warranted. If reconsideration is denied, the police department shall inform applicant of that decision in writing, setting forth in reasonable detail the reasons for the denial and shall inform the applicant of his right to appeal. Such appeal shall be before the city council in accordance with section 21-91. If an applicant desires to appeal a denial, the applicant must file a written request for an appeal with the city clerk within ten (10) business days of the date of the written notice informing the applicant of the denial of the license.
(k) Suspension, revocation of the license. Conviction for violating the provisions of this article or any other ordinance of the city, rules or regulations of the city or conviction for any felony or any crime involving theft, controlled substances, fraud or a crime against property shall subject the employee to immediate suspension or revocation of the employee permit, and in the case of the pawnshop establishment or the pawnbroker shall subject the license holder to suspension of any license authorized by this article.
(l) In all instances in which an application is denied, the applicant may not reapply for the same type of permit for at least one year from the date of denial.
(m) The annual personal identification card shall only be issued in the name of the individual applicant. All personal identification cards issued shall be granted for the full calendar year or for the number of months remaining in the calendar year. Any applicant granted a license before July 1 shall pay the full permit fee without proration. Permit fees for personal identification cards issued on or after July 1 shall be one-half (½) the annual permit fee. Permit fees are not refundable once the identification card is issued by the city.

1860:
(a) Any holder of a license to operate a pawnshop shall apply for renewal of an existing license and shall pay the annual license fee no later than February 15 th of each calendar year in which it does business.
